handbookNote: Louisiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017), published by the Louisiana Department of Public Safety & Corrections, Office of Motor Vehicles (OMV) -- fetched directly from https://dpsweb.dps.louisiana.gov/DPSForms.nsf/8bad5589175b8981862575f20048ee65/b49427def852192a862579a5004826d9/$FILE/68448863.pdf/CDL%20Driver%20Manual%20-July%202017%20r%200917.pdf on 2026-08-22 (5.3MB PDF, full text extracted via pdftotext -layout to scratchpad/la_cdl_research/la_cdl_manual_full.txt, 9,969 lines), supplemented by Louisiana Administrative Code Title 55 Part III (Third Party Tester provisions), fetched from https://expresslane.dps.louisiana.gov/Third%20Party%20Tester%20Forms/LouisianaAdministrativeCode.pdf on 2026-08-22 (extracted to scratchpad/la_cdl_research/la_admin_code.txt), and the official Louisiana OMV 'CDL Driver Education' page at https://expresslane.la.gov/omv/drivers/commercial-driver-s-licenses-cdl/cdl-driver-education/ (checked 2026-08-22) -- price matches this project's established CDL tier ($6.99). Real exam mechanics: NEITHER the base AAMVA manual, NOR the Louisiana Administrative Code Title 55 Third-Party-Tester provisions, NOR the official OMV CDL Driver Education webpage states an exact knowledge-test question count or number-correct-to-pass for any Louisiana CDL test (general knowledge or any endorsement) -- the OMV webpage explicitly defers to the CDL manual and a phone/contact-form inquiry for those specifics rather than publishing them itself. Several third-party test-prep sites claim '50 questions, 40 correct (80%) to pass, one hour time limit' for Louisiana's general knowledge test, but this figure could not be confirmed on any official LA.gov or dps.louisiana.gov source and is therefore NOT asserted as fact anywhere in this question bank -- per this project's no-default-values discipline, this is explicitly hedged rather than borrowed from another state or an unverified third party. What IS confirmed directly from official Louisiana sources: the federally standardized 80% minimum passing score applies (49 CFR 383.135(a), same as all other CDL-track states in this project); Louisiana has 5 classes of driver's license under R.S. 32:408 B.(2) and R.S. 32:405.1 -- Class A (combination vehicles, GCWR 26,001+ lbs with towed unit over 10,000 lbs GVWR), Class B (heavy straight vehicles, single vehicle GVWR 26,001+ lbs), Class C (small vehicles under 26,001 lbs GVWR that are either designed for 16+ passengers or carry placarded hazmat), Class D (chauffeur's license, non-CDL, age 17+), and Class E (personal vehicle, non-CDL, age 17+); CDL age minimums are 18 for intrastate and 21 for interstate commerce; the manual's own Section 1 text states there are 'six kinds of CDL endorsements' -- T (Double/Triple Trailers), P (Passenger), N (Tank Vehicle), H (Hazardous Materials, issued only to persons 21+), X (Combination Tank Vehicle + Hazmat), and S (School Bus) -- notably matching Indiana's six-endorsement set; the front-matter statute page additionally lists an 'M' Motorcycle endorsement, but this is a general driver's-license endorsement under R.S. 32:408(3) rather than one of the manual's six CDL-specific knowledge-test endorsements, and this distinction is preserved rather than conflated; only three endorsements (P, S, N) may be added to a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP), each paired with a mandatory companion restriction (P or S endorsement requires a P restriction; N endorsement requires an X restriction); there are ten standardized federal restriction codes (E, K, L, M, N, O, P, V, X, Z) plus at least one Louisiana-specific restriction code noted in the front matter ('55 - No 18-wheelers', added when a Class A combination vehicle's pulling unit is 26,000 lbs or less); initial CDL issuance requires a $15 application fee, a current DPSMV 2032 physical exam, proof of Louisiana residency/SSN/liability insurance, and results in a 180-day learner's permit upon passing the knowledge test(s); the hazmat endorsement requires a TSA fingerprint background check that must be within the most recent 180 days (via www.hazprints.com); Louisiana-specific CDL disqualification penalties include: 1 year CDL loss for a first BAC/DUI/refusal/felony offense, 3 years if the vehicle was placarded for hazardous materials, and a lifetime loss for a second such offense or for using a CMV to commit a felony involving controlled substances; a minimum 10-year disqualification from operating a school bus for refusing BAC testing or a DWI conviction in ANY vehicle (not just a CMV); 60 days CDL loss for two serious traffic violations in 3 years (120 days for three or more); 180 days CDL loss for a first out-of-service-order violation (1 year for a second within 10 years, 3 years for three or more -- the manual's PDF text shows a tracked-changes artifact rendering this as '90 180 days' for the first-offense figure, which this question bank resolves to 180 days as the surviving/current value, consistent with the federal standard in 49 CFR 383.51); and 60/120 days/1 year respectively for first/second/third railroad-highway grade crossing violations within 3 years. Content-depth rationale: Louisiana uses the AAMVA-authored 2005 CDL Testing System base manual (same generation as several other CDL-track states already built in this project) organized into the same 13 core sections as Indiana's manual -- Section 1 Introduction, Section 2 Driving Safely (by far the largest section), Section 3 Transporting Cargo Safely, Section 4 Transporting Passengers Safely, Section 5 Air Brakes, Section 6 Combination Vehicles, Section 7 Doubles and Triples, Section 8 Tank Vehicles, Section 9 Hazardous Materials (the second-largest section), Section 10 School Bus, Section 11 Vehicle Inspection (Pre-Trip), Section 12 Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, and Section 13 On-Road Driving -- plus Louisiana-specific statutory and administrative detail (license classes, endorsements, restrictions, disqualification penalties, fees) layered into the licensing bucket from the manual's own Louisiana-specific front matter. Some sections (Cargo, Tank Vehicles, Doubles/Triples) are naturally short in Louisiana's manual, and their question buckets were sized down accordingly rather than padded to match larger states. Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official Louisiana manual text or the supplementary official Louisiana sources cited in that question's source_note; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers.
